sentences.text: The name Ectenosaurus means "drawn-out lizard" because of its elongated muzzle.
This animal possessed a skull measuring about 64.5 cm in length and an estimated total body length of 5 to 6 meters.
It is characterized by prominent, elongated jaws that resemble those of the similar genera Plotosaurus and Pluridens.
Ectenosaurus had significantly smaller scales measuring 2.7×2.0 mm compared to the 3.8×4.4 mm scales of the similar-sized Platecarpus.
Fossil evidence suggests it moved with a rigid anterior torso propelled by a tail fin, rather than undulating its entire body like a snake.
The animal was originally described as Platecarpus clidastoides by John Campbell Merriam in 1894.
Dale A. Russell re-described the species as the new genus Ectenosaurus in his 1967 book Systematics and Morphology of American Mosasaurs.
In 2021, Willman, Konishi, and Caldwell designated specimen FHSM VP-401 as the neotype for E. clidastoides because the original type specimen was destroyed.
Kiernan and Ebersole named two new species, E. tlemonectes and E. shannoni, in 2023.
Ectenosaurus is classified within the Plioplatecarpinae subfamily of mosasaurs.
Fossils of Ectenosaurus are found in the Santonian and Campanian stages of Kansas, Alabama, and Texas.
Ectenosaurus lived between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago, from the Coniacian to the Campanian.
Stable isotope analysis shows Ectenosaurus was one of the few plioplatecarpines capable of living outside nearshore marine habitats.
Some scientific analyses suggest Ectenosaurus belongs to the mosasaurine group rather than the Plioplatecarpinae, showing close relations with Prognathodon.
